title: d3 evidence storage design recommendation
instruction:
You are Sgt. Ottilie Vanterpool, supervising District 3 evidence operations for the Sandhill Department of Natural Resources Conservation Law Enforcement Division. The state lab has told us that it will stop accepting long-term frozen storage on 1 December, and our 1974 field station is still holding tissue and DNA samples from open poaching and trafficking cases. Division Counsel Hollis Nakagawa needs a design she can attach to the capital request, and I need one buildable storage configuration, a price, and a defensible explanation of why the other workable candidates were set aside. The decision has to fit the station's existing electrical panel and slab, stay within the $180,000 capital cap, work with one designated custodian controlling access to the evidence, and remain defensible when the alarm-monitoring link drops during winter. Samples from federally charged cases are stored beside state-case samples but do not necessarily follow the same retention obligations. Heronbank Works is the likely contracting stakeholder, and the Sandpiper Board will review the capital request. Please write `district3_evidence_storage_design_recommendation.docx` and place it in the top level of the working directory, using exactly that filename. Make it a decision memorandum of no more than five pages, written for Hollis Nakagawa and Heronbank Works rather than for a general audience. Number the sections or recommendations so a reviewer can navigate them, but do not turn the memorandum into a system click-through or a construction drawing. Include a concise statement of the decision, a comparison of the serious alternatives you considered, an order-of-magnitude cost model, the assumptions behind any figures, the principal risks and mitigations, and an implementation path that covers the period before 1 December as well as the intended steady state afterward. Explain what happens when the normal storage, access, power, alarm, or retention process cannot be completed, including who records the exception and who decides whether evidence may be moved or released. Treat the federal and state retention distinction as a decision constraint rather than collapsing all samples into one category. Use exactly one recommendation, make the recommendation and its central cost figure agree everywhere in the memorandum, and end with the decision itself rather than a list of unowned next steps. You may estimate configuration and installation costs for planning, but label estimates and assumptions clearly; do not invent bids, statutory citations, agency policy numbers, or promises from Heronbank Works or the Sandpiper Board. Keep the focus on the storage design and its decision consequences, leaving out unrelated investigative tactics, laboratory analytical methods, and procurement-system instructions.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `district3_evidence_storage_design_recommendation.docx` — Decision memorandum recommending one buildable evidence-storage configuration for District 3's tissue and DNA samples. (top-level working-directory placement; maximum five pages; one recommendation only; must include alternatives, cost model, assumptions, risks, transition and end-state implementation, and exception handling; must be usable by legal counsel and a contracting stakeholder)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
DECISION MEMORANDUM
TO
FROM
DATE
SUBJECT
Hollis Nakagawa, Division Counsel
Heronbank Works, contracting stakeholder
Sgt. Ottilie Vanterpool
District 3 Evidence Operations
24 August 2026
District 3 frozen tissue and DNA storage configuration

1. DECISION AND SCOPE
Approve one on-site permanent configuration: a conditioned evidence room containing two independently powered, lockable upright -80 C freezers, each fitted with a local audible/visual alarm, continuous temperature logger, and battery-backed communications gateway. Allocate locked, clearly labeled racks within both cabinets to FEDERAL-CHARGED and STATE-CASE evidence; no rack, box, or inventory record may serve both categories. The planning total is $164,000, including contingency, below the $180,000 capital cap.
This memorandum deliberately treats the request as a permanent on-site build with a controlled bridge to it. It does not choose a temporary arrangement as the end state. The state laboratory will stop accepting long-term frozen storage on 1 December; continued reliance on its acceptance is therefore not a continuity plan. The 1974 field station also leaves the current evidence exposed to aging power, limited panel capacity, an unverified existing slab, and winter loss of the monitoring link.
2. BUILDABLE CONFIGURATION AND OPERATING CONTROLS
Install the two uprights in the existing former records room after a limited slab verification and, only if indicated, localized spreader plates/anchorage. This avoids a walk-in freezer’s concentrated load and large refrigeration start-up demand. Provide two dedicated 208/240-V circuits from the existing panel after field load measurement; specify staggered compressor restart and a listed load-management relay. The bridge is a 10-kW propane standby generator serving only the two freezer circuits, room lighting, gateway, and one receptacle. It is not a whole-station generator.
Planning environmental acceptance is -80 C operating setpoint, with each logger recording at least every 15 minutes. A warning is investigated at -70 C and an excursion response begins at -65 C or after any loss of logged data. These are design/operating assumptions for preservation planning, not a universal evidence or laboratory requirement. The room has a key-controlled door; each freezer has a separate mechanical key and electronic access log.
The designated Evidence Custodian alone holds normal keys and access authority. Every access record captures identity, purpose, time in/out, case/sample identifiers, cabinet/rack, and any movement. The custodian maintains a durable outer label and inventory location code: jurisdiction/case category, case number, item/sample number, freezer, rack, box, and retention-review flag. A supervisor may authorize one-time emergency access by a named alternate; the alternate signs the access and reconciliation record, and the custodian reviews it on return. There is no standing group keyholder list.
Federal-charged and state-case samples remain physically segregated by dedicated labeled racks and administratively segregated by category, case status, and review flag. Storage location does not decide retention. The custodian conducts a quarterly status review and an event review when charging, court, appeal, or case-status information changes; counsel/case authority confirms any retention consequence. No sample is released, disposed of, or moved out of controlled storage on an inventory review alone.
3. SERIOUS ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
Configuration
Planning cost / physical fit
Custody, alarm, retention consequence
Why set aside
A. Recommended: two -80 C uprights + conditioned room + limited standby
 $164k; two dedicated circuits after load test; slab verification/local remedy included.
Independent cabinets limit a single failure; rack segregation; local alarm and logged degraded mode.
Best combined fit under cap and on the 1974 station.
B. Single large walk-in -80 C room + standby
 $176k; technically feasible only with added structural/electrical confirmation.
One enclosure complicates isolated failure response; partitions can segregate categories.
Higher capacity/resilience is desirable, but little cap headroom and concentrated load/start-up risk.
C. Three compact -80 C uprights, no room conditioning
 $132k; lower slab/electrical burden; circuits still require field confirmation.
More cabinet redundancy, but exposed room conditions and tighter custody/segregation space; same link issue.
Lower-cost option set aside because the aging room is a greater environmental and access-control risk.
D. Hosted off-site frozen storage with transport controls
 $148k first-year planning allowance; avoids station slab/panel work.
Can segregate inventory, but transfer custody, retrieval delay, host access, and retention coordination add risk.
Not selected before 1 December absent a documented host acceptance and custody agreement.
E. Lease temporary portable freezer module + later permanent build
 $158k near-term bridge only; external power feed/site pad needed.
Can hold categories separately, but is a temporary operational arrangement with weather/transport exposure.
Useful contingency, not the selected end state; does not resolve permanent station controls.

All five configurations are technically plausible planning concepts, not bids. B and C are workable only after the same field checks; “feasible” does not make either the best capital decision. D becomes preferable only if a qualified host can document acceptance, custody terms, retrieval rights, and category-specific retention controls in time; none is assumed here.
4. ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE COST MODEL
Scope component
Planning estimate
Two lockable -80 C upright freezers; internal racks
 $48,000
Conditioned-room work, door, access hardware, signage
 $24,000
Dedicated circuits, load relay, disconnects, commissioning
 $18,000
Slab verification; allowance for local spreader plates/anchorage
 $9,000
10-kW propane standby, transfer equipment, limited branch work
 $29,000
Temperature loggers, local beacons/sirens, gateway, cabling
 $12,000
Move support, labels, custody reconciliation, acceptance test
 $6,000
Contingency for concealed 1974-station conditions
 $18,000
CENTRAL PLANNING TOTAL
 $164,000

Arithmetic: $48k + $24k + $18k + $9k + $29k + $12k + $6k + $18k = $164k. Local estimates are planning figures rather than bids or commitments by Heronbank Works or the Sandpiper Board. Assumptions: existing panel has capacity for two managed freezer circuits and limited generator transfer after a field load test; the records-room slab needs only the included local remedy; propane placement is permitted on the station site; and existing evidence volume can be allocated across two cabinets with 20% empty rack capacity. The cost uncertainty most capable of changing the decision is a discovered panel or service upgrade beyond the included branch work; the pre-award verification must price that condition before release of the contingency.
5. RISKS, DEGRADED MODE, AND EXCEPTION AUTHORITY
Risk / trigger
Immediate control and record
Owner / decision authority
Freezer fault or temperature at -65 C; sensor/logger data gap
Stop routine access; preserve local display/log; open an exception record; stage sealed inventory in the other cabinet only if capacity and condition permit.
Custodian records; Sgt. Vanterpool decides emergency internal move after case supervisor consults.
Utility loss or generator does not start
Confirm generator status; limit door openings; notify supervisor; use measured temperature trend to prioritize an authorized move.
Custodian records; Sgt. Vanterpool authorizes move.
Winter monitoring link drops
Local beacon/siren remains active; gateway marks communications lost; custodian performs and logs twice-daily local checks until link is restored.
Custodian records and notifies Sgt. Vanterpool; facilities contact investigates link.
Custodian unavailable; urgent access needed
Supervisor authorizes named alternate for one event; alternate logs identity, purpose, time, evidence, and two-person reconciliation.
Alternate records; Sgt. Vanterpool authorizes emergency access.
Retention status unclear, or release/disposition requested
Keep item in its category rack; flag record; do not release or dispose.
Custodian records; Hollis Nakagawa with the responsible case authority decides release/disposition.

Each exception record states trigger, affected identifiers, temperatures or alarm state, persons notified, action, authorization, and closure. Sgt. Vanterpool reviews open exceptions daily; the custodian closes an exception only after conditions, inventory, and logs are reconciled. A temporary location is rechecked every shift and must either return to approved storage or receive a renewed written decision within 72 hours. This prevents an emergency workaround from becoming informal permanent storage. Equipment service delay, failed sensor, or failed access hardware is treated through the same record and corrective-action path.
6. IMPLEMENTATION: BRIDGE TO 1 DECEMBER AND STEADY STATE
When / gate
Action and control
Owner
Now through 1 December (bridge)
Custodian freezes the baseline inventory; applies category/location labels; starts twice-daily manual temperature and access logs; identifies a controlled spare cabinet for emergency transfers. No new reliance on state-lab long-term acceptance.
Evidence Custodian; Sgt. Vanterpool
Before award
Heronbank Works validates panel load, circuit route, slab condition, room dimensions, generator siting, and freezer delivery path; price any condition beyond defined allowances for decision before commitment.
Heronbank Works; facilities reviewer; Sgt. Vanterpool
Installation / move
Keep current storage in service until new cabinets pass acceptance. Move sealed, logged lots one cabinet/rack at a time with custodian and witness; reconcile count, label, location, and temperature record at each handoff.
Custodian; designated witness; installer for equipment only
Before routine use (end state)
Acceptance check: setpoint stability; logger records; local beacon; simulated link loss; managed restart/generator test; access logs; federal/state rack labels; inventory reconciliation; exception form. Retain test records.
Custodian verifies; Sgt. Vanterpool accepts; Heronbank Works corrects installation defects
If permanent installation is late
Continue bridge controls and current storage; use only the identified controlled spare for a documented excursion. Escalate a need for external emergency storage to Sgt. Vanterpool and counsel; do not make an undocumented transfer.
Custodian records; Sgt. Vanterpool decides move; counsel advises on retention/custody consequence

7. DECISION
Approve the $164,000 planning configuration: two independently powered, lockable -80 C upright freezers in a conditioned, access-controlled District 3 evidence room, with limited standby power, local alarm capability, documented degraded-mode checks, and physically segregated federal-charged and state-case allocations. Authorize it subject to the bounded pre-award panel, slab, delivery-path, and generator-siting verification described above, while operating the pre-1 December bridge controls until the acceptance check is complete.

spec.professional_context: This is a capital-planning decision for a conservation-law-enforcement evidence facility. The document will be reviewed by division counsel and a contracting stakeholder before a capital request is prepared.
difficulty_sources: selecting one defensible configuration from several viable alternatives
balancing electrical, structural, custody, connectivity, retention, cost, and transition constraints
making explicit assumptions without presenting invented prices or legal requirements as facts
designing both a transition state and an end state, including an exception path

authoring_plan.purpose: Create a no-reference decision-memo task in which the solver must synthesize a defensible storage design from occupational knowledge, not retrieve a hidden answer.

solver_feasible_set.required_decision: Exactly one recommended configuration, with a single central planning cost below the $180,000 cap.
acceptable_readings: Interpret the ask primarily as an on-site permanent storage build with a transition bridge.
Interpret the ask as a near-term continuity design that uses a temporary controlled arrangement while the permanent end state is installed.
solver_feasible_set.requirement: Either reading is acceptable only if explicitly selected and consistently applied to the alternatives, cost, transition, and conclusion.

professional_constraints: The state lab stops accepting long-term frozen storage on 1 December.
The station is a 1974 field station with an existing electrical panel and slab that constrain installation.
One designated custodian must control keys and access authority.
Federally charged samples and state-case samples have different retention implications.
The task must cover both transition and end state.
The task must include an exception path for incomplete storage, access, power, alarm, or retention actions.

candidate_family: A robust new on-site low-temperature storage installation with dedicated resilience and controls.
A modular or distributed on-site configuration with lower structural or electrical burden.
A controlled off-site or hosted storage arrangement with transport and custody implications.
A staged transition configuration paired with a permanent end-state solution.
gold_construction.gold_expectation: The gold should not prescribe one exact product or price. It should contain one clearly preferred configuration, a coherent planning estimate, and three or more credible rejected alternatives whose rejection follows from the stated constraints.
gold_construction.cost_model: Use internally consistent invented planning estimates only, label them as estimates, include installation and meaningful contingency or explain exclusions, and keep the preferred total under the capital cap.
gold_construction.retention_model: Require physical or administrative segregation, case-status identification, controlled review, and authority-based movement or disposition without inventing statutes, policy numbers, or universal retention periods.
gold_construction.custody_model: Require a designated custodian, controlled delegation for absence or emergency, auditable access records, and documented reconciliation for any move.
gold_construction.alarm_power_model: Require a degraded-mode response for winter link loss and a power-loss response that is compatible with the panel constraint; do not claim perfect uptime.
gold_construction.transition_model: Include a pre-1 December control and a fallback if the permanent installation is delayed, then define the acceptance conditions for the end state.
gold_construction.exception_model: Specify immediate protective action, documentation owner, escalation, and decision authority for movement or release; include closure or review so exceptions do not become indefinite.
gold_construction.presentation_model: Keep the reference solution within five rendered pages, with a decision-first memo structure and no irrelevant investigative or laboratory content.

authoring_plan.reachability_check: All graded substantive criteria are professional expectations for evidence, facilities, custody, and decision writing. No exact vendor, statutory citation, private code, or hidden numeric answer is required. The two possible scope readings are intentionally allowed, while the $180,000 cap and 1 December deadline are explicit workplace facts.
